claim_boundary: Measured: every expired UUUU contract in the 2026-06-08..2026-08-21 window (294 series, 12 expiries, both rights). NOT measured: other underlyings, other windows, live (unexpired) contracts, other venues. The step from 'UUUU expired options' to 'US listed equity options generally' is an inference from the instrument class, supported by the CLc1 control, not a measurement. Also tested and excluded: the TR. field namespace (TR.SETTLEMENTPRICE is a futures field; TR.CLOSEPRICE is TRDPRC_1 re-served).

tr_namespace_probe._why: Web search surfaced TR.SETTLEMENTPRICE and TR.CLOSEPRICE as the documented route for historical settlement data. Both were tested; both are dead ends here.

lseg_official_example.note: LSEG's own worked example for EXPIRED options uses BID, ASK and TRDPRC_1 — no settle field. TR.PriceClose is used only for the UNDERLYING. Independent corroboration that expired equity options carry no settle here.
lseg_official_example.ric_suffix: confirms the expired suffix is the EXPIRATION month code + year, consistent with the measured ^F26-for-puts result

why_no_settle_exists.finding: There is no official closing or settlement price for US listed equity options — none is distributed by the options exchanges, by OPRA, or by the OCC. The field is absent from LSEG because the thing does not exist in the market.
why_no_settle_exists.consequence: Every end-of-day option mark is derived by whoever needs one. There are two documented industry approaches.

industry_methods.mechanical: closing bid/ask (midpoint) or the last print — LSEG already ships this as MID_PRICE / BID / ASK
industry_methods.theoretical: snapshot the quotes shortly before the close, fit a pricing surface, and read consistent marks off it — LSEG ships this as THEO_VALUE

why_no_settle_exists.note_for_AD9: The 'theoretical' method is precisely what this app's interpolated sheet does. Using THEO_VALUE as the mark AND drawing an interpolated sheet would be model-on-model; MID_PRICE keeps the mark market-derived so the sheet stays visibly the assumption (AD-9).
why_no_settle_exists.occ_settlement_is_different: The OCC 'settlement price' for equity options refers to the EXPIRATION settlement of the UNDERLYING (VWAP over the last 30 minutes on the primary exchange), used to decide exercise. It is not a daily mark for each option series.

mark_derivation.claim: LSEG's MID_PRICE is exactly the midpoint of the closing bid and ask — not a model.

holes_are_honest.note: No bid means no midpoint, so the mark is empty there — deep OTM contracts nobody will bid on. Those render as holes rather than being filled in (AD-9).
